title: Popular products pulled from Coles, Aldi, Costco and IGA this week - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia
text:
Product recall roundup: Snack sold at Coles, Costco, IGA, milk sold at Aldi, and baby toys - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia Search query for Search the web Search the web Skip to main 
 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Product recall roundup: Snack sold at Coles, Costco, IGA, milk sold at Aldi, and baby toys
 Regulators and retailers have issued several recalls over the last few days to protect Aussie consumers.
 Carina Stathis Sun 25 October 2026 at 10:46 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Customers are being urged to stop using several products recalled over the weekend .
 From two protein puddings sold at Coles, Costco, and IGA, to baby toys and an Aldi milk, the products were removed from shelves and websites immediately.
 Yahoo Lifestyle has gathered all the information worth noting to see if your product has been impacted.
 Items sold at leading supermarkets were recalled.
 (Getty) Pudding sold at Costco and Coles found with glass
 Two Arla puddings were recalled over the weekend as glass fragments were found in the food.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g) was available at Costco in New South Wales.
 Meanwhile, the Arla Protein Chocolate Flavour Pudding (200g) was sold at Coles in New South Wales and Queensland, as well as independent food retailers, including IGA and Supabarn in NSW and the ACT.
 Do you have a story? Contact carina.stathis@yahooinc.com 
 These two puddings were pulled from shelves at several supermarkets after glass was found.
 (FSANZ/Getty) The salted caramel flavour has a Best Before date of 28 April 2027, and the chocolate had a Best Before date of 9 May 2027.
 Consumers who bought the products with the above dates should not consume them and should return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Any consumers concerned about their health should seek medical advice," the recall on the Food Standards Australia and New Zealand (FSANZ) website reads.
 For further information, contact Arla Foods Mayer Australia on +61 2 9669 2211 or via email: enquiriescs@mayers.com.au

 Aldi Farmdale Long Life Milk with microbial spoilage
 Aldi also announced a recall of one of its milk products in two Aussie states.
 The supermarket issued an alert on Friday afternoon that its Farmdale Full Cream Long Life Milk 1L had been removed from shelves.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement FSANZ revealed the recall was due to microbial contamination (spoilage) detected in the product.
 Spoilage caused by microbes can mean that organisms have grown inside the milk when it should have been sterile.
 This long-life milk has been recalled due to microbial spoilage.
 (FSANZ/Yahoo Lifestyle) Affected batches of milk had a Best Before date of 5 June 2027 and were sold in Victoria and South Australia.
 "Consumers should not eat this product," FSANZ said. "Consumers should return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund.
 "Any consumers concerned about their health should seek medical advice."
 If you have any questions or need more information, you can contact Aldi's recall hotline on 1800 709 993. Alternatively, you can visit their website.
 Baby walker found on big-name retailer marketplaces
 A three-in-one baby walker sold on Kmart, Big W, Harvey Norman and Kogan's third-party marketplace was pulled from sale after failing to meet safety standards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sun Yee International issued a recall for the Playpals 3-in-1 baby walker because it "does not meet the performance requirements to prevent it from falling downstairs".
 This poses a risk of serious injury or death if the walker tips over, causing the baby to fall.
 Sun Yee International issued a recall for the Playpals 3-in-1 baby walker (pictured)
 (Getty/ACCC) Customers are urged to stop using the walker immediately and to keep it out of children's reach. The product was also sold on eBay and Lasoo.
 It has the SKU number of KID1029 and was sold nationally between 4 July 2025 and 7 October 2026.
 "Contact Sun Yee to arrange to return the walker for a free replacement with a compliant walker or a full refund," FSANZ said. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "If you have any questions or require assistance, please contact Sun Yee."
 To contact Sun Yee International Pty Ltd, call 03 9369 8588 on weekdays or email sales@sunyee.com.au . 
 Baby toy that could be a choking hazard
 A children's toy was also recalled on Friday as it didn't comply with safety standards for children up to three years of age.
 The Laughing Koala's Montessori UFO Pull & Pop toy was removed from the website because the silicone pull strings were too long and could pose a choking or asphyxiation risk.
 "Small parts may detach from the products and cause a child to choke if they place them in their mouth," the ACCC recall stated. 
 The Laughing Koala's Montessori UFO Pull & Pop toy was removed from the website (pictured)
 (Getty/ACCC) The model number is MT033516, and the product was sold from 8 November 2024, to 21 July 2026.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shoppers who bought the product are urged to stop using the toy immediately and place it out of reach of children.
 "Cut the pull strings of the toy and take a photograph of the toy before disposing of it in household waste," ACCC wrote.
 "Email the photograph and your order details to thelaughingkoala@hotmail.com to receive a full refund."
